newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse retreats, BUX futures plummet.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse retreats, BUX futures plummet.

text.p: Hungarian stocks retreated nearly one percent while BUX futures closed more substantially lower on Wednesday as a result of Tuesday's fall on Wall Street and of investors' wait-and-see attitude, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 5,137.54 points, down 40.59.
BUX futures fell for all maturities, by between 100.00 and 143.50 points. The nearest June BUX fell 140.00 to 5,360.5.
"The fall was due to Dow Jones' drop (on Tuesday) on one hand and to a wait-and-see stance on the other hand," said Robert Stalmayer of AB-Moneta Kft.
The Budapest bourse closes before Wall Street's opening.

Traders said a relatively low spot share turnover of 2.54 billion forints reflected the fact that many investors were on the sidelines waiting for the planned planned share issue in oil company MOL and first quarter corporate results.

On Wednesday chemicals TVK was heavy loser, weakening more than five percent to end at 2,105 forints, down 115. Traders said TVK's more than seven percent rally on Tuesday, propelled by domestic investors, made TVK's price attractive for profit-taking.

"Domestic investors pushed TVK's price up yesterday, making it attractive for foreigners to sell now," one trader said earlier today. "One reason is that foreign investors keep on selling the paper," another said.
Elsewhere on the market, financial stocks traded mixed.
OTP Bank losing 100 forints to finish at 3,440, Inter-Europa Bank rising 1,700 forints to 47,250, while shares in securities house Quaestor remained untraded.
Energy papers were also mixed, with gas distributor Primagaz gaining 405 forints to finish at 8,805, and MOL easing 20 to end at 3,010.
Retailer Csopak which said its management would propose the payout of a 10 percent dividen on 1996 results against an eight percent dividend last year, eased 115 forints to 2,975.
